name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
alias_note: The F0 build's manifest uses the tester-entered slug 'the-metropolitan-museum-of-art' (take 2026-09-20). Registry slug is 'met'; the alias keeps the two joinable.

location.footprint_note: The building is ~400 m long. Frames from one visit (2026-09-20) ranged 40.7784–40.7800 N, 73.9619–73.9635 W, all at 'the Met' — a single point with a small radius will misfile Egyptian-wing frames as 'outside'. Use a polygon or a ~250 m radius for the §4.1b prior.

collection_api.notes: Open, no key. Accession lookup is search with the number QUOTED: /search?q="49.11.4" returns exactly one objectID; unquoted, the same query returns 81,000 full-text hits. Then /objects/{id} carries accessionNumber, title, objectDate, objectBeginDate/EndDate, medium, creditLine, artistDisplayName, culture, period, department, GalleryNumber, objectURL. Verified 2026-09-20: 14 of 14 accessions from the first visit resolved to exactly one object each. GalleryNumber is a live display-state claim (§8.3), not a canonical fact — it says where the API thinks the object is, which the visit can contradict.

accession_formats.policy: LOCATE, DO NOT VALIDATE (D11, D21). Patterns rank candidates; nothing is rejected for failing them.

shapes.notes: Two-digit accession year, then lot, then item. The year runs from 1891 ('91') to 1974 ('74') in one gallery, so it cannot be used to order anything. Dominant shape.
Two components. Same family as above without the item number.
Same shape, large item numbers — bulk-accessioned collections (Cesnola 74.51.*, Moore 91.1.*). Longest tokens, most fragile to OCR.

accession_formats.locating_heuristic: In parentheses at the end of the credit line, immediately after the donation year: 'Rogers Fund, 1922 (22.139.24)'. The donation year and the accession's first component agree in 13 of 14 samples — 74.51.965 is credited '1874–76' — which is a useful confirmation signal, never a rule.
traps: Dates on Greek and Roman labels are BCE ranges written with an en dash — 'ca. 375–350 B.C.' — and on-device OCR offered '373-350' and '750-740' and '480-470' as accession candidates on three of fourteen labels. A date-range shape (two 3-digit numbers, a dash) needs to be scored DOWN as an accession, and the donation-year agreement above is what separates '750-740' from '74.51.965' on the same label.
Shared panels carry one credit line per object, each with its own accession in parentheses — three on the 'Three glass vessels' panel. One label, three primary keys.
Vitrines also carry small object tags with a bare accession ('91.1.1348', '601'), sometimes truncated by the tag edge. Same number, two surfaces.

labels.note: Two departments visited (Greek and Roman; Egyptian). Both use the same house card, so this is one dialect with a departmental variation, not two dialects in the MCNY sense. A loan card and a student-exhibition card are separate forms.

dialects.where: Greek and Roman galleries 151–158; Egyptian galleries 101–105, 132
dialects.typeface: serif (Times-like), black on white or on ochre (Greek and Roman)
field_order: title (bold) — an object description, not a name: 'Marble funerary lekythos of Aristomache'
culture, period / date: 'Greek, Attic, ca. 375–350 B.C.'
findspot or provenance line, optional: 'Said to have been found near the Kerameikos in Athens'
credit line, small type: 'Purchase, Joseph Pulitzer Bequest, 1949 (49.11.4)'
dialects.has_medium: in the title, not as a field — 'Marble …', 'Terracotta …', 'Glass …'. The API's medium field ('Marble, Pentelic') is richer than the label.
dialects.has_artist: rarely — 'Cesnola Painter' appears in the API but not on the label; the label leads with culture
dialects.notes: Antiquities labels have no artist and that is correct (D23). The 'title' is a descriptive phrase the museum wrote, so title matching against the API is exact but title matching against any other source is not.

field_order: credit line 'Lent by …' with no accession
dialects.notes: No accession at all — not the lender's, not the Met's. The degraded path (D17).

dialects.where: P.S. Art 2026, Uris Center for Education
dialects.notes: Names a minor. NOT PHOTOGRAPHED under the protocol; see docs/capture-protocol.md and data/README.md 'Minors'. Wall text and work only.

labels.photography_source: Welcome sign at the 81st Street entrance, 2026-09-20: 'Take photos: Just no flash or tripods, please.' Frames raw/2026-09-20-met/LCGW3693.JPG (app) and IMG_1356.HEIC (stock camera).
labels.lighting: Greek and Roman: bright, daylit, ochre cards under glass with reflections. Egyptian: dimmer, works behind glass, oblique angles unavoidable in vitrines.

access_rules_note: None captured first-hand. The admissions desk and any posted policy were not photographed on 2026-09-20; the field log records only 'Paid'. Do not fill this from memory or from a third party — the rule is the institution's own page or its own signage (§8.2).

provenance.source: first-hand visit, 2026-09-20, F0 collector's build (TestFlight, update 01a0bbb0) plus stock camera
provenance.source_image_note: Every frame carries GPS and a UTC offset — the first take where that's true. The app's frame of the welcome sign (LCGW3693) is out of focus and OCRs to garbage; the stock-camera frame reads clean. Rain limited exterior shots to the 81st Street side.

hours_note: Not observed. The 'hours_admission' frame in the manifest (f0039, EIZY6434) turned out to be the entrance sign, not an hours board.

accessibility.note: The entrance used on 2026-09-20 is signed with the wheelchair symbol (EIZY6434). The Fifth Avenue entrance is up the main steps. A reachability property (§6.6), separate from any admission concession.

display_state_observations.observation: P.S. Art 2026 on view in the Uris Center — 24th year of the exhibition, 19th at the Met, 125 works from ~1,000 submissions (exhibition wall text, OLOU4070).
display_state_observations.relevance: §8.3 — a temporary exhibition with no accession numbers and a labelling convention the house parser must not be applied to.

display_state_observations.observation: Gallery numbers from the API matched the walk for all 14 objects (158 → 152 → 151, then 101 → 105 → 132).
display_state_observations.relevance: Corroborates GalleryNumber as a usable display-state claim on this date.
